summary: Aurora Financial — sudden per-token billing spike and answer-quality regression during dedicated capacity rollback
description:
Issue summary:
Aurora Financial reported an unexpected, persistent spike in per-token billing on their enterprise account starting 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC, coincident with a measurable drop in answer quality (hallucinations on finance-specific prompts) and intermittent streaming disconnects. Impact: customer reported ~8x increase in apparent token usage for a subset of long-prompt inference flows and several production clients experienced incorrect financial-sounding outputs causing a temporary feature disablement.
Environment: production (us-east-1), Dedicated capacity pool: aurora-prod-1, pinned model redwood-llama-70b-v1 with fallback to rw-qa-ensemble-v2.
Steps observed / reproduce attempt:
1) Customer performed a canary rollback of a dedicated pool config at ~02:10 UTC (autoscale policy change).
2) From ~02:15 UTC, their monitored per-token charges spiked; internal metrics showed sudden increase in average sequence lengths and repeated KV-cache misses.
3) At the same time, automated QA alerts flagged higher hallucination rates for finance prompts.
4) Streaming clients intermittently received socket resets (~02:20–02:45 UTC).
Logs / Evidence:
- Grafana billing dashboard: spike in BilledTokens for account aurora-fin-acc (link redacted).
- Serving runtime logs: repeated LRU eviction warnings and "cache-miss-forwarding" events for the aurora pool.
- Traces: several requests routed to rw-qa-ensemble-v2 fallback during peak (trace IDs listed in investigation notes).
- Customer-provided transcripts showing incorrect numeric assertions and invented bank names.
Business impact:
- Customer disabled product feature for ~45 minutes; estimated revenue exposure and regulatory risk given wrong financial assertions.
- Customer escalated to Enterprise CS manager immediately and requested root-cause + credits for excess billing.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) - 2026-03-10:02:55 UTC: Observed autoscaler churn events and a backlog of queued requests to aurora-prod-1. Pushing temp throttle to protect downstream billing. Opening INC-20260310-A1.

Priya Sinha (Runtime Eng) - 2026-03-10:03:30 UTC: Noted that a new kernel selection fallback introduced in PR #1824 may produce longer tokenization in edge cases for finance prompts. Investigating commit for side-effects on caching keys.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) - 2026-03-10:04:20 UTC: Temporarily pinned serving to pre-PR model variant and forced pool warmup. Early telemetry shows token counts returning to baseline for test traffic.
Priya Sinha (Runtime Eng) - 2026-03-10:09:12 UTC: Deployed hotfix to prevent cache key changes during rollback window (rollback of kernel-selection flag). Monitoring for quality regressions.

Maya Patel (Support Engineer) - 2026-03-10:12:00 UTC: Customer confirmed feature restored with improved outputs; requested formal postmortem and bill adjustment. Raised SUP-62905 to track billing credit workflow.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) - 2026-03-11:10:05 UTC: Added follow-up action items for autoscaler policy guardrails and improved canary playbook. Draft postmortem attached to Confluence.
Elena Roarke (Aurora) - 2026-03-11:18:30 UTC: Thanks for quick mitigation. We'll review client-side telemetry and coordinate acceptance of proposed credits.
investigation_notes: Timeline reconstruction: 02:08–02:11 UTC customer initiated a pool config rollback; 02:12–02:20 UTC internal autoscaler began scaling down followed by rapid scale-up events as tokens queued; 02:15–02:40 UTC billing spike observed; 02:20–03:00 UTC intermittent streaming resets correlated with load spikes.

Hypothesis A: Cache-key incompatibility after kernel-selection logic change caused repeated recomputation of full context leading to inflated billed token counts and higher model entropy (quality regression). Evidence: 'cache-miss-forwarding' events and increase in mean input sequence lengths in traces where fallback was used.

Hypothesis B: Autoscaler race during rollback caused request duplication or replays in the warmup window leading to duplicated billing attribution. Evidence: duplicate trace IDs and backlog counters incremented during scale operations.
Telemetry snippets: request-id list: trace-97a4, trace-97a5, trace-97a6 (routes showing fallback to rw-qa-ensemble-v2), Grafana panels attached to Confluence page.

Related code change: runtime PR #1824 introduced a heuristic that changes tokenization boundary handling for certain numeric sequences; reverted in emergency hotfix PR #1831. See https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824 and /pull/1831.
Customer-supplied artifacts: sample prompts + outputs uploaded to support bucket (S3 URI redacted).
resolution:
Mitigation: pinned Aurora's dedicated pool to pre-change model variant and applied hotfix to restore previous cache key behavior; applied temporary throttling to the pool to prevent autoscaler thrash. Outcome: token billing returned to baseline within 25 minutes and hallucination alerts subsided. Billing: Support and Finance approved a proactive credit for excess billed tokens pending Aurora acceptance.
Root cause: combination of (1) a runtime kernel-selection heuristic change that altered cache key semantics causing repeated full-context recomputation for some finance prompts and (2) an autoscaler race during a rapid config rollback which amplified request load and produced transient duplication. Both factors needed for observed magnitude of billing spike and quality regression.
